title: Docker Container Runtime Architecture
summary: The Docker CLI drives the daemon and containerd; runc builds the container from image layers using namespaces, cgroups, a bridge network and volumes.

nodes.label: Docker CLI
nodes.detail: Sends commands such as run or build to the Docker daemon over a socket.

nodes.label: dockerd
nodes.detail: Manages images, networks and volumes, and delegates container lifecycle to containerd.

nodes.label: containerd
nodes.detail: Pulls images, manages snapshots and starts containers through a runtime shim.

nodes.label: runc
nodes.detail: Creates the container process using Linux primitives, then exits; the shim stays to supervise it.

nodes.label: Image Layers
nodes.detail: Images are stacked read-only layers shared between containers. A thin writable layer sits on top via overlayfs.

nodes.label: Namespaces + cgroups
nodes.detail: Namespaces isolate PID, network, mount and more. cgroups cap CPU, memory and I/O for the container.

nodes.label: docker0 Bridge
nodes.detail: Linux bridge connecting container veth pairs. NAT rules provide outbound access and published ports.

nodes.label: Container
nodes.detail: Application process running with its own root filesystem, network namespace and resource limits.

nodes.label: Volume
nodes.detail: Directory managed outside the writable layer, so data survives container removal and can be shared.

steps.title: CLI calls the daemon
steps.text: docker run is sent to dockerd, which resolves the image and network settings.

steps.title: containerd prepares a rootfs
steps.text: containerd pulls missing layers and builds an overlay snapshot as the container filesystem.

steps.title: runc creates the process
steps.text: runc applies namespaces and cgroups, then starts the entrypoint process.

steps.title: Networking is attached
steps.text: A veth pair connects the container's network namespace to the docker0 bridge.

steps.title: Volumes persist data
steps.text: Mounted volumes store data outside the writable layer so it outlives the container.
